NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI semiconductor value chain, acting as a fabless designer that is critically dependent on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and SK Hynix for HBM memory, while commanding extraordinary pricing power over hyperscaler and enterprise customers who have few viable alternatives for high-performance AI training and inference accelerators. Its dominant software ecosystem (CUDA) creates deep switching costs downstream, while its concentration of manufacturing at TSMC and geographic exposure to Taiwan represents the primary upstream supply chain risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a fabless designer that outsources chip fabrication primarily to TSMC while sourcing displays, memory, and components from a concentrated group of Asian and domestic suppliers. On the downstream side, Apple sells through carrier partners, its own retail ecosystem, and enterprise channels, while its high-margin Services segment is increasingly underpinned by platform fees and licensing deals with major digital economy players like Google and Meta.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain, converting advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and specialty materials from upstream capital equipment vendors (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) into DRAM, NAND, and HBM products sold to hyperscalers, AI accelerator vendors, and mobile OEMs. Its downstream exposure is increasingly shifting toward high-value AI infrastructure customers like NVIDIA (HBM) and major cloud providers, even as it maintains broad diversification across mobile, automotive, and client PC end markets.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the center of the global semiconductor ecosystem, generating revenue primarily through IP licensing and royalties rather than physical manufacturing, making its downstream customer relationships with chip designers and hyperscalers its most critical value drivers. Its upstream dependencies are largely limited to EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys needed for IP development, giving ARM exceptional gross margins (~95%) and significant leverage over the industry given that ARM-based chips power over 99% of the world's smartphones.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company that sits at the intersection of data center, networking, and storage infrastructure, relying heavily on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and ARM/EDA vendors for its design ecosystem. Its downstream position is increasingly oriented toward hyperscale cloud customers like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft who commission custom AI and networking ASICs, making Marvell a critical enabler of data center silicon customization.
